summary: North Carolina household of 3 adults (all in their thirties), renters, no children, no one pregnant, over 65, disabled, or a full-time student, and no other income. Reported household work income is $950,000 to $1,300,000 a year (confirmed twice). At that income, none of the ten programmes apply: SNAP, TANF, SSI, Medicaid, CHIP, school meals, and the ACA premium tax credit are all income-tested far below this level; EITC is zero at this income and childless; the child tax credit requires qualifying children, and WIC requires a pregnant person, postpartum person, infant, or child under 5. Assets were not reported; they would not change the result. If the income figure was actually monthly (about $950 to $1,300 a month, roughly $11,400 to $15,600 a year), the household could qualify for SNAP and NC Medicaid, and this should be re-screened.
